assertions.name: H₂O lones are symmetric (equal defects), H₂S lones are asymmetric
assertions.source: H₂O (s,s) defects equal; H₂S (s,p) defects 0 vs 2 — self-dual vs chiral lone

description: The H₂S +2.1° residual is a lone-pair braid-word asymmetry. H₂O's two lone pairs are equivalent self-dual e⁻=σ₀σ₁σ₀ (palindromic defect 0,0 — symmetric). H₂S's are inequivalent: the inert 3s² (self-dual, defect 0) and the 3p_z (chiral, non-palindrome, defect 2ℓ=2). The defect mismatch (0 vs 2) is the asymmetry; the chiral p-lone's directional bias opens the orbital-locked 90° base. The asymmetry exists iff the s-channel is inert (pure-p, third row) — H₂O (s active) has none.

data.finding: The H₂S +2.1° is a braid-word asymmetry between its two lone pairs: the inert 3s² is the self-dual e⁻ (palindromic defect 0, ℓ=0), the 3p_z is chiral (defect 2, ℓ=1). H₂O has two EQUAL self-dual lones (defects 0,0) — symmetric, no tilt, clean 104.5°. The defect mismatch (0 vs 2) in H₂S — present only because the s-channel is inert (pure-p, third row) — gives the chiral p-lone a directional bias that opens the orbital-locked 90° base by ~+2°. So the residual is the structural signature of the inert s-pair, not a fit; exact magnitude needs the chiral-lone directional-repulsion model.
